title: A study plan
hook: write what, when, and with whom
tomorrow: Saba turns eighty on Sunday. what does the Mishnah say eighty is for?

segments.voice: That was a week of learning for life: a teacher saying it again, a note in the margin, a question left standing, a doubt said out loud, honey on the letters, and a day of rest. Yesterday's line: rest from study too.
screen: `REST FROM STUDY TOO.` → `A WEEK OF LEARNING FOR LIFE.`

segments.voice: A brand-new planner on the first day of school, every page clean, every intention huge. A few weeks later, the pages are blank. A plan like that doesn't fail from lack of wanting. It fails from someday. Hillel saw that coming. In Pirkei Avot he warns: don't say, when I have free time I'll study, because you may never have free time.
screen: `EVERY PAGE CLEAN.` → `PLANS FAIL FROM SOMEDAY.` → `YOU MAY NEVER HAVE FREE TIME.`

segments.voice: Shammai, the sage so often named beside Hillel, gives the other half in the same book: make your Torah study a fixed thing. The Hebrew word is keva, set, regular, the opposite of whenever. So a study plan doesn't need to be big. It needs three answers. What: one text, the portion, a page of Talmud, a Psalm, a book you chose for next year. When: a time that already exists in your week, after dinner on Tuesdays, the train on Monday morning. With whom: a chavruta, a study partner, a class, a cousin, or a parent at the kitchen table. Everything from this week fits inside it. Plan to teach what you learn. Leave room in the margin for your own notes. Keep a list of the questions left. Let doubt come to the table. Expect some sweetness. And write the rest into the plan, too: Shabbat is in the calendar on purpose. Something to tell a friend tonight: Pirkei Avot sets Hillel and Shammai side by side on this one: a plan beats someday.
screen: `SHAMMAI: MAKE IT FIXED.` · `WHAT. WHEN. WITH WHOM.` · `THE WEEK FITS INSIDE IT.` · `WRITE IN THE REST, TOO.` · then, large: `A PLAN TO KEEP LEARNING.`

segments.voice: Write three short lines. What: one text you'd like to keep learning. When: one time that already exists in your week. With whom: one name, even if it's only your own. Read the three lines back once; that's the plan.
A study plan: what, when and with whom. Shammai's fixed time, against Hillel's warning about someday.
Your line: a plan to keep learning, because free time may never come. That's the study stretch, done.

chat.meaning: Shammai says make your study fixed; Hillel warns that free time may never come. A small plan with a time and a partner keeps learning going.

Hillel.meaning: a sage of the Mishnah's early era, often paired with Shammai

Shammai.meaning: a sage often paired, and in debate, with Hillel

chavruta.meaning: a study partner; learning in pairs

Pirkei Avot.meaning: a book of the Mishnah collecting the sages' sayings
